VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
items.excerpt: Visual agents must turn video observations into timely decisions to track progress and choose what to do next. Building on the emerging System One paradigm, we introduce VideoJev, a family of models that cast video understanding and interaction as structured decision tasks. We adapt pretrained multimodal large language models (MLLMs) by replacing autoregressive answer decoding with a shared head that scores temporal intervals and textual options against video evidence. These scores yield event spans or answer choices, unifying temporal grounding and multiple-choice video question answering. This combines the semantic flexibility of MLLMs with efficient decisions that agents can use directly. As an interaction unfolds, new goals and intermediate results prompt further queries about the same visual history. VideoJev therefore reuses visual computation through Cached inference for queries as they arrive and Joint inference for multiple queries in a single forward pass. Across three temporal grounding benchmarks, VideoJev-4B and VideoJev-35B-A3B improve mean mIoU over their backbones by 6.7 and 10.8 points, respectively, with measured inference speedups of $2.8$-$3.1\times$. On four video QA benchmarks, both achieve performance comparable to their backbones in Thinking mode, with measured inference speedups exceeding $100\times$. These results offer a unified, reusable decision interface for composing structured visual judgments into complex, open-ended workflows.
items.summary: 本文提出 VideoJev 系列模型，将视频理解与交互建模为结构化决策任务，通过用共享打分头替换预训练多模态大语言模型的自回归答案解码，对时间区间和文本选项进行评分，并采用 Cached 与 Joint 推理复用视觉计算。据原文，该模型在三个时间定位基准上较其骨干模型分别提升平均 mIoU 6.7 和 10.8 点、实测推理加速 2.8 至 3.1 倍，在四个视频问答基准上 Thinking 模式下性能与骨干模型相当且实测加速超过 100 倍；这些结果提供统一可复用的决策接口，但具体性能数字来自论文报告，公开材料未说明其独立验证或适用范围限制。

items.title: Jellyfish-Inspired Hydrogels Enabling Synergistic Antifouling and Low-Drift for Transformer-Assisted Multimodal Marine Bioelectronics
items.excerpt: ABSTRACT Hydrogels have emerged as a versatile materials platform for soft and biointegrated electronics. However, reliable hydrogel bioelectronics under seawater conditions is limited by biofouling at interfaces, high-salinity swelling-induced drift, and noise-robust temporal decoding. Here, we present a hydration-locked percolation strategy to engineer a jellyfish-inspired hydrogel that combines synergistic antifouling with drift-resistant conduction for AI-assisted multimodal marine bioelectronics. The constructed hydration-polyphenol network suppresses nonspecific adsorption and early biofilm evolution, achieving a synergistic antifouling system that repels and inactivates fouling organisms. Meanwhile, cross-substrate wet anchoring and localized swelling suppression stabilize electron-percolation pathways, thereby enabling long-term stable high conductivity (22 S m − 1 ) and physiological signal acquisition with high signal-to-noise ratio in seawater. Notably, a tailored multimodal decoding framework integrating Transformer encoder with multilayer perceptron further enables accurate interpretation of complex physiological signals (98.5% accuracy) by capturing long-range temporal dependencies and cross-modal correlations. This integration of high-performance bioinspired hydrogels with Transformer-assisted decoding paves the way for long-term, high-fidelity marine bioelectronics.

items.title: A Transferable Machine-Learned Potential Enabling Large-Scale Copper-Carbon Simulations from Equilibrium to Extreme Conditions
items.excerpt: Cu-C materials and interfaces are central to diamond thermal management, metallization, graphene growth and carbon-coating technologies, but atomistic simulations across these applications require a potential that describes metallic Cu, diverse carbon bonding, heterogeneous Cu-C interactions and close atomic encounters. Here we develop NEP-CuC, a transferable neuroevolution potential trained on a dataset of 2,727 uniformly relabelled configurations selected from a heterogeneous Cu-C candidate pool. Disagreement within an ensemble of five independently trained models provides an internal indicator of model sensitivity. A Ziegler-Biersack-Littmark (ZBL) correction describes short-range nuclear repulsion, while a runtime D3(BJ) correction supplements dispersion-sensitive calculations. Tests on source-derived held-out and independent external datasets, together with structural, elastic, defect, interfacial, vibrational and finite-temperature transport benchmarks, establish broad but property-dependent physical fidelity across elemental Cu, diverse carbon environments and heterogeneous Cu-C configurations. Large-scale simulations of amorphous-carbon formation and orientation-dependent shock compression of Cu further test transferability under strongly non-equilibrium conditions. For Cu/diamond interfaces, the same potential describes deposition, annealing and tensile response: preparation history leaves persistent differences in interphase structure, while the mean peak nominal tensile stress at 500 K decreases from $12.35\pm0.71$ to $6.65\pm0.98$ GPa as the incident Cu energy during the initial deposition stage increases from 1 to 50 eV. NEP-CuC provides an atomistic framework for linking processing, interfacial structure and physical response across Cu-C systems, with direct relevance to Cu/diamond thermal-management interfaces, diamond metallization and non-equilibrium Cu-C processing.
items.summary: 本文开发了NEP-CuC神经演化势，基于2,727个统一重新标注的Cu-C构型训练，并引入ZBL短程核排斥修正和运行时D3(BJ)色散修正，在源数据留出集和外部数据集及多种平衡与非平衡基准上评估其可迁移性。该势为跨Cu-C体系的原子尺度模拟提供了连接工艺、界面结构与物理响应的框架，可用于Cu/金刚石热管理界面、金刚石金属化和非平衡Cu-C过程研究，但原文明确指出其物理保真度是广泛而依赖具体性质的，外部测试误差还包含域外迁移与参考协议差异。

items.title: Complex materials engineering via Provenance Action Graphs: potential, structure and demonstration
items.excerpt: This work discusses and tests the potential of reaction graphs for material synthesis, in which events consist of reaction steps (actions) and their outputs (observations). The importance comes from the requirement to synthesize technologically useful materials, especially those that are kinetically stabilized. Often, it is a science that follows years of trial and error, culminating in (published) successful recipes, but is truly driven by far more (unpublished) failures. The entry into the era of AI provides an opportunity to use learning algorithms to encode rules from multi-dimensional synthesis pathways, regardless of their technological usefulness, and to decode both forward prediction and inverse learning modes. The main incentive is to accelerate material discovery by generating a global knowledge base that can be shared among data agents and contributed to by them. We will focus on several scenarios in the common synthesis process during solid-state synthesis, primarily because these reactions are kinetic in nature and require closer monitoring and control of the reaction history.
items.summary: 本文提出并验证用“溯源动作图”将材料合成中的反应步骤与观测结果建模为事件图，以便借助AI从多维合成路径（尤其固态合成）中学习正向预测与逆向设计规则、构建可共享知识库，从而加速动力学稳定材料的发现与制备。

items.title: Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations by Correcting Modality Misrouting in Omnimodal LLMs
items.excerpt: Omnimodal large language models (OLLMs) are susceptible to cross-modal hallucinations under audio-visual interference. We find that, for a substantial fraction of incorrect joint predictions, the question-relevant unimodal branch can still recover the correct answer, suggesting that task-relevant evidence can remain recoverable from the relevant modality even when it is not reflected in the joint prediction. We refer to this recoverable failure pattern as \emph{modality misrouting}. We propose CaRe (Conflict-aware Residual Intervention), a training-free inference-time method for identifying and correcting modality misrouting. CaRe uses a text-only modality probe to identify a candidate modality-specific counterfactual branch, and flags potential misrouting when its prediction conflicts with the original joint prediction. For such cases, CaRe computes a residual direction from the discrepancy between the counterfactual and fused representations and uses it to steer the original multimodal state toward the relevant modality evidence, while retaining both modalities in the original audio-visual inference path. The intervention strength is adapted based on the confidence of the counterfactual branch. Experiments on CMM and AVHBench across two OLLMs show that CaRe consistently outperforms the evaluated inference-time hallucination-mitigation baselines.
items.summary: 本文提出一种免训练的推理时方法CaRe，通过文本模态探针识别模态特定反事实分支、检测其与联合预测的冲突，并利用反事实与融合表示间的残差方向引导多模态状态，以纠正跨模态幻觉中的模态误路由。该方法在CMM和AVHBench上对两个全模态大语言模型进行了实验，作者报告其优于所评估的推理时幻觉缓解基线，但摘要未给出具体性能数字，且现有材料不足以支持对该方法在其他模型或任务上的泛化性作出结论。

items.title: Can Machine Learning Potentials Be More Accurate Than the Methods They Are Trained On?
items.excerpt: Although machine learning potentials (MLPs) generalize across configurational and chemical compound spaces, their accuracy is commonly believed to be limited by their training methods, with improvements beyond this limit achieved so far only by refitting to experimental observables. In this Perspective, we argue that MLPs can also be made more accurate than their training methods non-empirically by generalizing across a third space, that of quantum-chemical methods. We propose routes to method-transferable MLPs that predict at unseen methods, with working implementations in both density-functional and wavefunction-based theories showing that they can be more accurate than any of their training methods. Aiming beyond the accuracy of the training methods could also make universal MLPs more accurate than single-method models, even when the method-transferable MLPs remain less accurate than those QM methods. Method-transferable MLPs will shape the construction of training datasets and the evaluation of models, pushing the accuracy limits of chemical simulations.
items.summary: 本文提出“方法可迁移机器学习势”的思路，主张通过跨量子化学方法空间泛化，使机器学习势能在未见方法上预测，并可比任一训练方法更准确。若该方法可推广，将影响训练数据集构建与模型评估，并可能提升化学模拟的精度上限；但相关结论来自Perspective论述与已展示的实现，其普适性和性能边界仍需进一步验证。

items.title: Knowledge-Guided Construction of Machine Learning Potentials for Reactive Behavior in Energetic Materials
items.excerpt: Energetic materials involve multiple interactions, making reliable machine-learning potentials (MLPs) difficult to construct without extensive datasets. Here, we enhance the ability of the neural network interatomic potential (NNAP) to describe molecular systems using sphmulti, a refined spherical-harmonic basis set that combines extra radial basis with element-specific chemical weighting in each radial channel. We further integrate hyperactive learning, farthest-point sampling, and iterative sufficiency criteria with knowledge-guided key events, enabling the NNAP to retain essential information for describing the material system. For 3,3'-diamino-4,4'-azoxyfurazan, the resulting NNAP is trained on only 13,680 configurations yet captures key properties, including the isomerization barrier, pyrolysis activation energy, and shock Hugoniot behavior. NNAP-driven molecular dynamics simulations further reveal that pyrolysis proceeds through furazan-ring opening followed by chain reactions, whereas shock loading induces anisotropic hydrogen transfer driven by interlayer structural deformations. This work enables efficient and reliable MLPs for energetic materials.
items.summary: 本文通过改进球谐基组（sphmulti）并结合超活跃学习、最远点采样与迭代充分性判据，构建了能描述含能材料反应行为的神经网络原子间势（NNAP），并在3,3'-二氨基-4,4'-偶氮氧化呋咱上以13,680个构型完成训练。该工作为含能材料提供了一条高效构建机器学习势的途径，但相关性能仅在原文所报告的这一体系与性质范围内得到展示，尚需针对其他材料体系进一步验证。

items.title: Interaction-as-a-Judge
items.excerpt: Coding agents are tasked with producing sophisticated interactive applications such as websites, desktop applications, and games. While humans assess these applications interactively, current automated LLM evaluations primarily focus on code analysis and unit tests. This mismatch can cause LLM judges to miss failures that are immediately apparent to human users. We study Interaction-as-a-Judge, an evaluation paradigm where computer-use agents (CUAs) directly interact with an application. We demonstrate that Interaction-as-a-Judge can improve both \emph{evaluation} and \emph{generation} of interactive applications. To this end, we collect and release two complementary datasets: $6,858$ pairs of applications with human preferences and corresponding agent traces, and $222$ applications with human-verified requirement labels. Relative to standard non-interactive approaches, we find that Interaction-as-a-Judge improves evaluation in terms of predicting human preferences ($65.6\% \to 69.1\%$) and requirement verification ($77.0\% \to 81.6\%$). We also observe scaling benefits: across both preference alignment and requirement verification, higher-quality interactions improve performance. Finally, through both inference- and training-time experiments, we demonstrate that Interaction-as-a-Judge can also improve the quality of generated artifacts. At inference time, Interaction-as-a-Judge repairs $75.5\%$ of broken requirements within five attempts, compared to $55.4\%$ for code-only self-feedback. At training time, using Interaction-as-a-Judge as a reward signal improves win-rate over the base model by $6.7$pp while reducing both generated code length by $35.7\%$ and build failure rates by $7.2$pp compared to a code-only reward signal.
items.summary: 本文提出以计算机使用智能体直接与应用交互的Interaction-as-a-Judge评测范式，并构建了包含6858对带人类偏好及智能体轨迹的应用和222个带人工核验需求标签应用的数据集，用于对比其与非交互式方法的评测与生成效果。该工作可用于交互式应用的偏好预测、需求核验与生成改进研究；但相关改进幅度均来自作者报告，尚需独立验证，且摘要未说明任务范围与适用边界。

items.title: Training LLMs for Multi-Agent Collaboration with Verifiable Information Rewards
items.excerpt: Effective collaboration among large language model (LLM) agents in multi-agent systems requires sharing relevant evidence, requesting missing information, and incorporating teammates' contributions into decisions. Training these behaviors is challenging because final task outcomes provide limited feedback on the value of individual messages. We introduce CoSIR (Collaboration via Surprisal-based Information Rewards), a post-training approach that uses a simple, verifiable environment to teach collaboration behaviors that generalize to more complex, unseen tasks. We propose a Bayesian evaluator that scores shared information by its reduction in team surprisal, defined as the sum of the negative log probabilities assigned to the correct option given each agent's available evidence. Requests are scored by the potential reduction in the same quantity if the requested information were truthfully provided. Separate rewards encourage agents to use the received information in their private choices and calculations. We post-train Qwen3-4B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-3-4B-it through self-play and evaluate transfer to seven unseen natural-language collaboration tasks. CoSIR achieves the highest aggregate score, while its performance in general tasks remains competitive. Behavioral analyses show increased disclosure of private evidence and fewer judged failures to use teammates' input.
items.summary: 本文提出CoSIR后训练方法，利用可验证环境和贝叶斯评估器，按共享信息对团队惊讶度的降低及请求信息的潜在降低分别给予奖励，并训练智能体在私有决策中使用所获信息。该方法在Qwen3-4B、Qwen3-8B和Gemma-3-4B-it上经自博弈后训练，并在七个未见自然语言协作任务上评估迁移效果，但材料未说明其在一般任务上的绝对性能或普适性限制。

items.title: Learning from fracture: Teaching language models to design through physical experience
items.excerpt: How can language models learn to optimize physical designs through experience? We introduce FracLearn, an experience-abstraction-generalization framework evaluated through a deliberately unfamiliar, Tetris-inspired fracture game. The model first proposes architectures and examines simulated fracture responses to accumulate experience. Abstraction organizes these observations into conditional principles linking reinforcement placement, crack evolution and load transfer, with supporting evidence and failure conditions. Generalization challenges the model to combine these principles in new architectures and surpass the earlier design record. Campaigns demonstrate progressive refinement and recovery through hypothesis revision, yielding a best composite score 11.0% above the experience-stage record. Fracture analyses connect improved performance to crack deflection and temporary trapping as toughening mechanisms, alongside greater residual load capacity. Learning occurs through external knowledge and decisions, without model-weight updates. This approach offers a route to scientific agents that turn computational experiments into reusable physical knowledge for materials discovery and engineering design.
items.summary: 本文提出 FracLearn 框架，让语言模型通过“设计—模拟断裂—抽象原理—泛化组合”的经验循环，在无需更新模型权重的情况下优化物理设计，并在类俄罗斯方块断裂游戏中将最佳复合得分较经验阶段纪录提升 11.0%。

items.title: Coupled Harness--Model Evolution for Scientific Equation Discovery
items.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to discover scientific equations from experimental data. Such a discovery system has two parts that must work together: a library of executable computational tools and the model's tool-use policy. The tools supply the solving capability, from diagnosing structure in the data to fitting candidate equations; the policy plans and orchestrates their use. Yet existing systems adapt only one part, keeping either the toolset or the model fixed, which leaves the corresponding failures uncorrectable. We develop a coupled evolution framework that improves both parts from the same verifiable fit-error signal. In the tool-evolution phase, an agent grows an executable tool library from a small set of generic numerical operations by diagnosing its own failures: it authors a new tool when a capability is missing and revises its selection rules when the right tool went unused. In the policy-evolution phase, a small open model (roughly 3B active parameters) is fine-tuned on successful tool-use trajectories collected with the frozen library, on training formulas screened to be disjoint from all evaluation benchmarks. Ablations show the two phases are complementary: with no tool library at all the same model solves almost nothing, the tools account for most of the gain, and trajectory training adds a further gain that is largest on the most difficult problems. The full system solves 79.1/71.3\% of LSR-Synth problems at fit tolerances $10^{-2}$/$10^{-3}$, reaches 63.8\% pooled accuracy on the distributionally different SRSD-Feynman panel, and obtains a normalized CP3-28 aggregate of $-7.27$. These results suggest a broader recipe for scientific agents: let the model and its instruments improve each other under verifiable feedback.
items.summary: 该论文提出一种利用同一可验证拟合误差信号协同进化工具库与模型工具使用策略的耦合演化框架，使二者相互改进，从而显著提升大语言模型从实验数据中发现科学方程的能力。

items.title: Humanize Olympiad Agents: A Multi-Session Workflow for Olympiad Problem Solving with Solve, Review, Wiki, Verify
items.excerpt: Large language model (LLM) agents are rapidly improving on long-horizon scientific and olympiad tasks. Recent systems have produced a Lean-formalized resolution of the Navier--Stokes problem and autonomous solutions to four open questions in the Erd\H{o}s Conjectures database. Yet neither system releases both its underlying model and complete inference stack. More broadly, a single agent session remains brittle on difficult problems: early errors can propagate, missing domain knowledge can stall progress, and apparent success can mask a misinterpretation or weakening of the original task. We introduce HOA (Humanize Olympiads Agent), an open, flow-level framework that coordinates multiple agent sessions through three complementary feedback channels. First, an independent reviewer evaluates each candidate and provides actionable feedback. Second, a structured wiki supplies task-specific knowledge that may be missing or unreliable in model pretraining. Third, a verifier checks generated Lean proofs against trusted challenge statements. With GPT-5.6 Sol, HOA achieves perfect scores on the IMO, IPhO, and IOI 2026, near-full marks on the IChO 2026 problem set, and solves all 672 problems (100%) on PutnamBench. On the Lean-Eval leaderboard, HOA ranks first, solving 251 of 304 problems (82.6%). We further evaluate HOA with open models. Using Kimi-K3, HOA achieves full scores on the IMO, IPhO, and IOI, and a gold-level score of 97.1% on the IChO. These results closely match the closed-source GPT-5.6 Sol + /Goal baseline on the IMO and IPhO, while exceeding it on the IChO and IOI, demonstrating that systematic feedback can help bridge substantial differences in base-model capability.
items.summary: 本文提出开源多会话工作流 HOA，通过求解、独立评审、结构化 Wiki 和 Lean 验证器三条反馈通道协同多个 LLM 智能体会话，在 IMO、IPhO、IOI、IChO 2026、PutnamBench 与 Lean-Eval 等奥赛及数学基准上取得近满分或领先表现，表明系统性反馈能显著提升长程奥赛问题求解能力并弥合基座模型差距。

items.title: MatQuery: Execution-Grounded Natural-Language Querying over Heterogeneous Materials Databases
items.excerpt: Materials scientists increasingly combine information from several public databases, each with its own interface, schema, units and calculation conventions. MatQuery is a prototype and experimental infrastructure for studying how a natural-language request can be turned into queries over such databases and how the returned values can be interpreted. This report describes what has been built and the preliminary results obtained so far. The prototype holds frozen, self-verifying local copies of six public materials databases (about 10,000 records each), a catalog of declared fields derived from them, a database-independent query representation with an adapter for each database, and an eight-step pipeline in which a language model proposes and deterministic program steps check, execute and assemble. A benchmark generator produces questions whose reference queries are verified by execution on the frozen copies and whose wording is checked by back-translation and review. An evaluation harness runs direct prompting, CHESS and Alpha-SQL on the same frozen basis. Preliminary experiments on an 800-question development set show that direct generation with three demonstrations reaches 82.4% strict execution accuracy (56.5% without demonstrations), that a low-cost scorer selects the exact set of databases for 85.0% of complete requests with well-calibrated probabilities, and that band gaps differ by more than 0.5 eV in 31.6% of composition-matched cross-database clusters. Two pilots show the limits of the current approach: a probe-then-ask policy gave answers rated valid by both reviewers in only 11 of 50 sessions, and only 115 of 300 sampled record pairs could be compared by structure. The complete pipeline is in smoke testing and has not yet been evaluated at scale.
items.summary: TLDR：MatQuery 是一个“执行验证”的自然语言查询原型基础设施，通过大模型提议与确定性程序校验、执行和组装，将跨六个异构材料数据库的请求转化为可执行查询并解释结果，初步在 800 题开发集上达到 82.4% 的严格执行准确率。

items.title: Masked Diffusion Language Agents for Tool-Integrated Chemical Reasoning
items.excerpt: Designing tool-integrated reasoning agent systems for complex chemical tasks remains a fundamental challenge. Although recent chemical agents have demonstrated promising performance through the integration of external tools, they are still built on the autoregressive paradigm, which is inherently constrained by causal attention and left-to-right generation. As a result, they often struggle with bidirectional molecular understanding, global coordinated tool planning and multi-source evidence integration. To address this challenge, we introduce ChemDiffAgent, the first masked diffusion language agent for tool-integrated chemical reasoning. It reformulates chemical reasoning as iterative denoising over interleaved reasoning and tool-use trajectories, enabling tool-use decisions to be jointly determined under full-trajectory context and thereby better aligning the agent's decision boundary with its knowledge boundary. We further analyze how this paradigm benefits agentic reasoning through harder infilling subproblems during training and flexible arbitrary-order decoding during inference. Then we develop a two-stage post-training framework, comprising agentic supervised fine-tuning and variance-reduced preference optimization, to enhance tool-use and reasoning capabilities. We also construct a comprehensive benchmark covering six chemistry tasks across both single-turn and multi-turn tool-use scenarios. Under matched budgets and evaluation, ChemDiffAgent consistently outperforms autoregressive agents, achieving an overall improvement of approximately 20%. Notably, our 8B model achieves performance comparable to, in some cases surpassing, significantly larger frontier models, such as GPT 5.5 and Claude Opus 4.7. Code is available at https://github.com/bilemond/ChemDiffAgent.
items.summary: 本文提出首个用于工具集成化学推理的掩码扩散语言代理 ChemDiffAgent，将推理与工具使用轨迹重构为迭代去噪过程，并借助两阶段后训练，在六项化学任务上较自回归代理平均提升约20%，使8B模型表现可比甚至超越GPT-5.5、Claude Opus 4.7等更大模型。

items.title: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Automated Tuning of Specialized Neural Network Models
items.excerpt: Many machine learning approaches are two-level: an expert selects a class of methods, within this class the choice of key components is critical and usually manual. This paper addresses the automatic tuning of these components and proposes a framework transferable across models of different nature. The multi-agent large language model (LLM) framework has three roles---analyst, coder, and recorder~---with an experiment log and a sandboxed execution environment. Unlike systems that optimize the entire ML script or search architectures in a discrete space, the framework operates over an open but semantically narrow space: the agent generates code only for the specified components, leaving the overall network structure unchanged. The approach is validated in two directions: tuning a classification spiking neural network with correlation learning, and solving high-order differential equations with Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINN). Across five tasks---spiking classification on MNIST and Digits, and boundary-value problems for the generalized nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation (GNLSE) and Kuramoto--Sivashinsky (KS) equations---the agent outperforms the baselines: classification accuracy is 13 percentage points (MNIST) and 6 percentage points (Digits) higher; the error against the analytical single-soliton solution is reduced approximately 2491-fold; the invariant-preservation error drops approximately 325-fold in the selected GNLSE run with a Gaussian perturbation and by more than 100-fold on average over repeated initializations; and the mass drift drops 14-fold for the KS problem with a Gaussian perturbation. The framework thus tunes key components on tasks of different nature without changing its internal structure.

items.title: Provenance-grouped protocol for evaluating machine learning in perovskite photovoltaics
items.excerpt: Machine-learning models for perovskite solar cells are typically evaluated using random data splits, which we show systematically leak information through massive internal duplication. Because nearly two-thirds of curated devices share their exact recipe with another, random splits primarily reward the mere recall of historical data rather than testing true physical generalisation. To solve this, we mapped the institutional provenance of the Perovskite Database and established a rigorous hierarchy of grouped splits that progressively isolate duplicate devices, publications, and institutions. Benchmarking thirteen models establishes new state-of-the-art performance across all splits and reveals a critical regime shift: while tree ensembles dominate random splits by recognising familiar recipes, their ranking collapses on genuinely unseen institutions and future discoveries, where composition-aware neural architectures excel. Furthermore, feature importance demonstrates that the device architecture and fabrication methodology dictate final efficiency just as strongly as the absorber chemistry. This standardised protocol empowers the community to separate memorisation from true physical discovery.

items.title: Hindsight Structured Advice Distillation: Steering Executor Agents with Advisors Trained on Their Failures and Task Characteristics
items.excerpt: Language-model agents are used for specialized work such as financial research, healthcare and law. Such agents are often capable enough for a task but still miss its details. In finance, for example, these details include which filing reports a figure or how a company discloses a metric. Retraining the agent to learn these details is expensive, and often impossible when the agent is a closed or shared system. Writing the missing know-how into the agent's prompt makes the prompt long and identical for every input, although different inputs need different guidance. We propose to learn to generate this guidance instead. A small advisor model reads each input and writes structured advice, which is appended to the prompt of a frozen executor. The advisor is trained with hindsight, following work on distillation with privileged information. On a training pool with graded answers, we analyse the executor's failures, run it under several strategies to see which one worked on each input, and let a teacher that sees the grades and the traces write the advice that would have helped. The advisor then learns, by supervised fine-tuning, to write that advice from the input alone. Because the student is a separate small model rather than the executor, it is cheap to train and adds little latency. We call this approach hindsight structured advice distillation (HSAD). On FrontierFinance, a public benchmark of expert-written financial research queries, an 8B advisor raises the qualification rate of Samaya's proprietary research agent, which already leads the benchmark's leaderboard, from 52.9% to 56.6%. This is above the agent's own high-effort configuration, at 37% lower cost per query. We study the generalization of the proposed approach, and in particular show that HSAD also improves results on WebShop, BIRD text-to-SQL and ExpertLongBench.

items.title: Faithful and Complete LLM-Assisted Automated Construction of Hierarchical Hardware Knowledge Graphs
items.excerpt: Hardware datasheets contain engineering specifications essential for component selection, system integration, and hardware compatibility verification. However, manual inspection is tedious and error-prone because datasheets are lengthy and heterogeneous, with dense information fragmented across tables, figures, and text. Although large language models (LLMs) can automate this process, na\"ive one-shot processing omits relevant specifications even when the document fits within the model's context window. We present an automated LLM-driven pipeline that transforms hardware datasheets into general-purpose hierarchical hardware knowledge graphs through chunk-based property extraction, hierarchical routing, and iterative refinement. The framework uses LLMs for information extraction and semantic reasoning while preserving source provenance and applying graph updates through validated instructions and deterministic local execution. This staged design reduces per-query context and maintains traceable intermediate representations. The resulting knowledge graphs provide semantically organized, source-grounded hardware properties for downstream retrieval and reasoning. We evaluate the framework on 20 hardware datasheets spanning diverse component types and document lengths. We assess property faithfulness and introduce inter-graph completeness to measure relative semantic coverage without exhaustive ground truth. Our framework achieves 98.8% property faithfulness compared with 76.1% for the one-shot baseline, while fully covering 83.6% of faithful baseline properties; in the reverse direction, the baseline fully covers only 10.5% of ours. These improvements provide more reliable and comprehensive engineering information for downstream hardware design and verification, reducing the risk of overlooked constraints and incorrect decisions.
items.summary: 本文提出一种基于大语言模型的自动化流水线，通过分块属性提取、分层路由和迭代优化，将硬件数据手册构建为可溯源的分层硬件知识图谱，在20个数据手册上实现了98.8%的属性忠实度，并显著优于一次性处理基线（76.1%）。

items.title: Critical Mass: Structure-Disjoint Splits Drift With the Libraries They Are Built On
items.excerpt: Molecular machine learning evaluates out-of-distribution performance with structure disjoint splits, a construction rule fixed once at the scale its library happened to have: threshold a pairwise distance, then assign whole connected components to folds. For predicting structures from mass spectra, the field has converged on single-linkage clustering under the myopic Maximum Common Edge Subgraph (MCES) distance at a threshold of 10. This convention was set on 29,000 molecules but public libraries now hold 227,690 molecules. MCES is NP-hard per pair over a quadratically growing set, and so the criterion has never been evaluated at that scale. We propose an optimized version of this criterion, allowing for computationally feasible application on the public libraries: Admissible bounds and a union-find skip reduce $2.6 \times 10^{10}$ molecular pairs to only $1.15 \times 10^{7}$ integer programs, a $2{,}259\times$ saving, while provably producing the lossless partition. We find that at this scale the graph percolates. A single component holds $95.5\%$ of the library, capping any test set at $4.5\%$. What remains is not merely smaller, but systematically different: a held-out compound outweighs a training compound 88.1\% of the time, because a fixed absolute budget is a tighter relative tolerance on a larger molecule. Large library benchmarks using this splitting rule naively therefore conflate structural novelty with extrapolation to larger, more complex chemistry.
items.summary: 该研究提出可扩展优化方法，首次在22.7万分子公共库上评估质谱分子机器学习常用的MCES距离阈值10结构不相交划分，发现图会渗流（最大连通分量占95.5%，测试集至多4.5%），且留出分子比训练分子更大的概率达88.1%，说明该固定划分规则会随库规模增长而漂移，将结构新颖性与向更大更复杂化学的外推混为一谈。

items.title: Collaborative Learning and Reasoning over Model Slices
items.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) excel across diverse tasks, benefiting from knowledge priors, in-context reasoning, and test-time computation. Despite these strengths, single-model reasoning remains vulnerable to error propagation, as later steps depend on the model's earlier outputs, leaving reasoning blind spots difficult to independently reassess. To address this limitation, we develop \textit{collaborative learning}, encompassing the construction of heterogeneous collaborators and the learning of effective cross-model collaboration. Specifically, \textit{model slicing} replaces a large model with smaller, heterogeneous models under a comparable parameter budget, enabling prior reasoning to be reassessed across distinct model parameterizations. \textit{Pyramid supervision} combines protocol distillation with step-level supervision to refine reasoning and interaction decisions throughout collaboration. We evaluate our approach across four task categories: multi-hop question answering, mathematical reasoning, code generation, and open-ended constrained generation. The trained heterogeneous models achieve comparable or better task performance than the original large model and established multi-agent baselines, including reinforcement-learning-based methods, while also achieving higher inference efficiency than the multi-agent baselines and exhibiting differentiated collaboration patterns across tasks. These findings show that learned collaboration turns model heterogeneity into complementary reasoning capabilities.
items.summary: 该论文提出通过“模型切片”将大模型替换为同等参数预算下的异构小模型，并用“金字塔监督”学习跨模型协作，从而把模型异构性转化为互补推理能力，在多种任务上以更高推理效率达到或超越原大模型及多智能体基线。

items.title: CB-Orchestrator: Adaptive Workflow Optimization for LLM Agents via Contextual Bandits
items.excerpt: Large Language Model (LLM) agents have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in tackling complex tasks through agentic workflows. However, manually designing these workflows is labor-intensive and lacks flexibility to adapt to diverse queries. While automated workflow optimization is a promising direction, existing methods often incur expensive API costs during training-phase feedback collection. Furthermore, they fail to adaptively reuse high-quality workflows, which creates a bottleneck for both performance and cost-effectiveness. To address these limitations, we propose CB-Orchestrator, an adaptive framework that decouples workflow generation from selection. In the first stage, we construct a diverse pool of candidate workflows via evolutionary search. In the second stage, we formulate workflow selection as a Contextual Bandit problem, which enables sample-efficient learning by balancing exploration and exploitation, thereby significantly reducing the feedback required for training. During inference, the model adaptively selects the optimal workflow tailored to each query. Evaluations across five diverse benchmarks demonstrate that CB-Orchestrator consistently outperforms all baselines. Notably, on the MATH dataset, CB-Orchestrator achieves better performance than strong recent baselines while reducing training-phase API token overhead by no less than 40.55% and total end-to-end training (including workflow pool generation) token overhead by no less than 29.73%.
items.summary: CB-Orchestrator 提出将 LLM 智能体工作流生成与选择解耦的自适应框架：先用进化搜索构建候选工作流池，再用上下文赌博机按查询高效选择最优工作流，从而在多项基准上提升性能并显著降低训练及端到端 API token 开销。

items.title: SpireBench: Evaluating Long-Horizon Strategic Play of Agentic Models with Slay the Spire
items.excerpt: Agentic large language models now tackle complex tasks, yet strategic reasoning over long horizons is under-studied: most agentic benchmarks are short and episodic, and performance on long tasks is hard to dissect into stored knowledge, reasoning and luck. We introduce SpireBench, in which models play the complete commercial deck-builder Slay the Spire (StS), where early decisions decide long-term success. Across 20 large language models (LLMs) at the game's highest difficulty, frontier models beat heuristic baselines and match the average human player but remain far behind experts. This gap widens as the run lengthens: the strongest models win the first act as often as experts, then fall behind. What separates strong models from weak is how well they play each fight; all of them misjudge risk over a run, preserving health rather than spending it to grow stronger. A comprehensive, self-consistent renaming of every game term shows that part of their performance rests on prior knowledge of the game, and models do not improve from the memories they write across runs, which are often wrong and overly cautious. Our harness is the first to give a model the complete original game, and we compare it with existing harnesses. Overall, SpireBench offers an unsaturated long-horizon benchmark with tools to locate where and why agents fail.
items.summary: SpireBench 让 20 个 LLM 在最高难度下完整游玩《杀戮尖塔》，发现其长时程策略表现虽超过启发式基线、接近普通人类却远逊专家，且随游戏推进差距扩大，根源在于战斗决策与风险误判、过度保守以及无法从跨局记忆改进，从而提供了一个可定位智能体长时程失败原因的未饱和基准。

items.title: VIGOR: Verifiable Industrial Geometry Optimization and Repair in Scene Programs
items.excerpt: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly generate structured layouts and executable scene programs from natural-language instructions. However, executability does not imply engineering feasibility: an industrial scene program may execute successfully while its final state still violates coupled boundary, collision, clearance, aisle, or structural constraints. We identify this mismatch as the executability-engineering-feasibility gap, where locally plausible placements can remain globally infeasible because corrections to one device may introduce violations elsewhere. To make this gap measurable in a controlled setting, we construct an execution-grounded industrial scene-program dataset with 1,749 constructible scenarios, complete executable programs, and 94 final-state geometric checks per scenario. We further propose VIGOR, which combines supervised scene-program generation with execution-grounded verification and staged geometric refinement. Supervised fine-tuning establishes complete program generation, local projection resolves independently correctable violations, and joint conflict-graph repair coordinates residual multi-object conflicts while preserving structural relations. Experiments show that VIGOR achieves 96.86% Complete Feasibility and an Overall score of 91.20, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 10.42 points in Overall. These results show that, under controlled industrial layout conditions, reliable scene-program generation requires not only executable programs, but also explicit verification and coordinated resolution of coupled engineering constraints.
items.summary: 本文提出 VIGOR，通过监督式场景程序生成、执行验证与分阶段几何修复来弥合工业场景程序“可执行但工程不可行”的差距，在 1,749 个场景上达到 96.86% 完整可行性并显著优于基线。

items.title: EliteTable: Self-Improving Program Search for Executable Control Policies
items.excerpt: EliteTable is a self-improving program-search algorithm guided by large language models (LLMs) that uses a fixed-capacity table of high-scoring solutions to guide new proposals, edits of existing solutions, and remixes of several solutions. Performance was evaluated across six Gymnasium control tasks, each with ten generations and fifty candidate slots per generation. Each task was evaluated across ten independently initialized searches. Candidate-score medians rose between the first and final generations in all six tasks, and selected-winner search-score medians rose in five. In CartPole-v1, the selected winner reached the search-score ceiling in the first generation of all ten searches. All ten paired held-out endpoints improved in four of the six tasks. BipedalWalker-v3 and CarRacing-v3 improved without reaching their reporting targets. Six of ten Acrobot-v1 searches declined on held-out episodes, and the median paired change was negative. The results document improvement during program search and the transfer of selected-winner gains to new episodes in some tasks. Comparisons and ablations are needed to establish EliteTable's relative performance and the contributions of its components.

items.title: Humanize MLE Agents: Multi-Agent Session Alternation Beyond Single-Agent Limits
items.excerpt: Existing LLM-based agent approaches for long-horizon machine learning engineering (MLE) often use context engineering, implemented through custom harnesses that manage tools, skills, and accumulated experience. However, we find that as single-session execution lengthens, the agent's reasoning intensity declines alongside slowing progress, summarized as long-horizon deceleration, and the benefits of these custom harnesses vanish as the underlying model improves, summarized as harness staleness. These findings suggest that their benefits may not persist across versions, which motivates a workflow-level approach in which agents build on one another's work across sessions. We model these alternating agent sessions as a context-reset semi-Markov decision process (CR-SMDP) and establish sufficient conditions for alternation to exceed single-agent reference limits, derive an explicit experiment-budget bound, and characterize when session caps preserve this advantage. Guided by this analysis, we introduce Humanize MLE Agents (HMA), which alternates two agents on a shared workspace, limits each session to at most k experiments and resets the context between sessions, without additional task-specific harness or prior knowledge supplements. Across 75 Kaggle tasks in MLE-bench, HMA reaches a state-of-the-art any-medal rate of 78.2%, exceeding the strongest open-source baseline by 8.0 points with a quarter of its time budget. Moreover, among six configurations spanning five heterogeneous agent pairs, HMA improves any-medal rate over the constituent baselines by 6.4 points on average, demonstrating cross-pair generality. A supplementary case on kernel optimization reaches 878 cycles, within 1.6% of the community leaderboard leader, demonstrating applicability beyond MLE.
items.summary: 这篇论文提出 Humanize MLE Agents（HMA），通过两个智能体在共享工作区交替会话、限制每轮实验数并重置上下文，克服单智能体长时 MLE 的推理减速与 harness 过时问题，在 MLE-bench 的 75 个 Kaggle 任务上以 1/4 时间预算达到 78.2% any-medal 的 SOTA，并验证了跨智能体组合与 kernel 优化任务的泛化性。

items.title: RATED: Reliability-Aware AI Agent Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics
items.excerpt: As AI agents increasingly rely on external tools, accurate retrieval is essential for reliable behavior. Existing methods optimize semantic relevance but largely ignore tool availability during execution. To address this gap, we propose RATED (Reliability-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution Dynamics), a retrieval framework that combines robust semantic matching with dynamic reliability adaptation. RATED employs a frozen dual-encoder with contrastive fine-tuning for semantic matching, and a lightweight contextual bandit module that re-ranks candidates based on real-time execution feedback. This design enables rapid adaptation to runtime tool failures without expensive model retraining. We introduce EcoAgent, a benchmark of 5,172 real-world tools and over 210,000 query-tool pairs for offline retrieval and dynamic reliability evaluation. Experimental results demonstrate that RATED achieves a 52.2% relative MRR improvement over the ToolLLM API retriever on real-world queries, and reduces fault selection rate from 86.2% to 2.9% under severe API outage scenarios with a 30% failure rate, while incurring negligible latency overhead of less than 1 ms over encode-only inference. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/Elliotes/EcoAgent.
items.summary: 该论文提出 RATED——一种结合语义匹配与基于执行反馈的动态可靠性重排的 AI 智能体工具检索框架，可在无需重新训练的情况下快速适应运行时工具故障，并在真实查询和严重 API 故障场景中显著提升检索可靠性。

items.title: Quality, Not Just Outcome: A Structural Scoring Framework for Selecting Coding-Agent Trajectories for Supervised Fine-Tuning
items.excerpt: Open coding agents are commonly trained through supervised fine-tuning on interaction trajectories whose final patches pass the benchmark test suite. However, this outcome-level filtering criterion ignores process quality: trajectories that eventually succeed may still contain inefficient interaction patterns such as repetitive file inspection, unstable tool usage, or delayed modification behavior, all of which become part of the imitation target. We propose TQS (Trajectory Quality Score), a structural scoring framework for coding-agent trajectories that operates directly on trajectory structure, requires no LLM judge, and runs in linear time. TQS characterizes trajectory quality through structural signals organized around structured convergence: information focus, intent--action alignment, and policy dynamics. Using 155,144 successful trajectories from a public open-license corpus, we rank trajectories by TQS and fine-tune coding agents on filtered subsets. Models trained on top-ranked trajectories consistently outperform those trained on random or bottom-ranked subsets on SWE-Bench-Verified. Our results suggest that process-level trajectory quality is an important factor in coding-agent supervision and that structural trajectory filtering provides an effective and scalable alternative to LLM-based data selection.
items.summary: 提出无需LLM评判、线性时间运行的结构化轨迹质量评分框架TQS，从信息聚焦、意图-行动对齐和策略动态等过程信号筛选编码代理的成功轨迹用于监督微调，在SWE-Bench-Verified上优于随机或低质量轨迹训练，表明过程质量而非仅最终结果对编码代理监督至关重要。

items.title: Quantitative Eshelby stability: local and finite-shape theory through AI-assisted mechanics
items.excerpt: How can human researchers use artificial intelligence (AI) to make progress on difficult mechanics problems while retaining control of physical significance, mathematical rigor, and validation? We explore this opportunity through a quantitative stability problem rooted in the Eshelby conjecture. For a uniform dilatational eigenstrain in a homogeneous isotropic solid, we establish a nonlinear two-sided relation between whole-interior strain heterogeneity and a geometry-only distance from the ellipsoid family, with half-order Sobolev scaling that captures morphological length scale. We then develop a complementary finite-shape theory: ellipsoidal subtraction yields an exact residual-field budget from which systematically convergent upper and lower bounds are obtained for a prescribed geometry. Applied to protruded, indented, and necked inclusions, the bounds agree with independent displacement-based finite-element calculations. The study also documents a human-led, AI-assisted research process in which researchers select consequential problems, shape targets, audit arguments, require independent checks, and interpret mechanics, while AI broadens analytical exploration and supports computation. This experience also led us to develop Open Problems in Mechanics, a versioned community-facing map that makes selected mechanics questions, their known/open boundaries, and criteria for progress explicit.
items.summary: 本文以AI辅助力学方式研究Eshelby猜想中的定量稳定性，建立了内部应变非均匀性与偏离椭球族几何距离之间的局部非线性双向关系及可收敛上下界的有限形状理论，并用有限元验证，同时展示了人类主导、AI辅助扩展探索的研究范式。

items.title: JANUS: Enhancing Long-Horizon Autonomous Research with Co-Evolving World Models
items.excerpt: Long-horizon autonomous research has shown promise in accelerating scientific progress through sustained cycles of hypothesis generation, implementation, and validation. However, this Generate-Execute-Feedback paradigm relies on reactive trial-and-error, where costly and time-consuming executions introduce severe feedback delays, throttling evolutionary progress under explosively expanding search space. To address this challenge, we propose JANUS, a framework that unifies future outcomes forecasting and past experience reflection through a Predict-Verify-Evolve loop driven by a co-evolving world model. Within an evolving graph, the research agent proposes candidates while world model scores them by forecasting value improvement, information gain, and exploration utility, then accordingly selects, refines, or prunes branches prior to execution. After receiving ground-truth feedback, JANUS distills experience into evolving skills: hierarchical skills for research agent, exploration-strategy skills for world model, and their coordination protocols. This mechanism enables continual co-evolution: the research agent sharpens candidate generation while the world model refines its predictive judgment over extended horizons. Extensive evaluations on MLS-Bench-Lite and real research tasks demonstrate that JANUS significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving both higher evolving efficiency and ceiling.
items.summary: 本文提出 JANUS，通过共同演化世界模型驱动的“预测-验证-演化”闭环，在执行前评估并筛选研究候选，并利用真实反馈持续蒸馏技能，使研究智能体与世界模型协同进化，从而显著提升长周期自主研究的效率与上限。

items.title: Open-o3-Video-v2: Seek, Ground, and Reason with Verifiable Spatio-Temporal Evidence
items.excerpt: Reliable video reasoning requires models to produce correct answers and expose supporting visual evidence. Open-o3-Video enables verifiable reasoning by embedding timestamps and object-level bounding boxes into reasoning traces, but is restricted to frames from an initial sparse sampler. We introduce Open-o3-Video-v2, which formulates video reasoning as a unified agentic evidencegrounded process. The model identifies missing information, acquires additional observations, grounds the moments and objects supporting its reasoning, and writes this evidence into the trajectory before continuing or answering. To support this behavior, we construct STGR-v2-CoT135K, including 52K multi-turn agentic grounded reasoning trajectories, and STGR-v2-RL-13K for reinforcement learning. We further propose Clue-Seek GRPO (CS-GRPO), which tracks how tool calls change accumulated evidence, rewards clue coverage and step-wise gains, and penalizes excessive, repetitive, or uninformative retrieval. On V-STaR, Open-o3-Video-v2-4B achieves 40.4% mAM and 56.3% mLGM, outperforming its Qwen3-VL-4B backbone by 8.5% and 12.6%, respectively. It also delivers consistent gains across general video understanding, long-video reasoning, and temporal grounding benchmarks. These results show that active evidence acquisition and verifiable object-level grounding are complementary for reliable video reasoning. The code and models are released at https://msalab-pku.github.io/projects/Open-o3-Video-v2.
items.summary: 本文提出Open-o3-Video-v2，将视频推理建模为统一的智能体证据接地过程，使模型能识别缺失信息、主动获取额外观察并将关键时间戳和物体边界框写入推理轨迹，同时构建了STGR-v2-CoT135K和STGR-v2-RL-13K数据集并提出Clue-Seek GRPO训练方法。该工作面向需要可验证时空证据的视频推理研究，其报告的性能提升仅在特定基准和基线比较下成立，需以原文公开的评测条件为准，且不构成对通用场景下性能的已验证结论。

items.title: The 3rd International Workshop on Artificial Intelligence for the Science of Science
items.excerpt: Over the past decade, the field of artificial intelligence (AI) has witnessed significant advancements across various domains, such as natural language processing and computer vision, which have further accelerated discoveries, innovations, and breakthroughs in many interdisciplinary fields — including Science of Science, which relies on big data to uncover reproducible patterns governing the evolution of research topics, collaboration networks, knowledge diffusion, and the systemic factors that drive scientific progress. Today, Science of Science is incorporating AI techniques into the analysis of big data, yielding deep and compelling insights into both longstanding and emerging problems in the field. Building on the success of the first and second AI4SciSci workshops, held in conjunction with ICDM’23 and JCDL’25, respectively, we propose the Third International Workshop on Artificial Intelligence for the Science of Science (AI4SciSci) to further engage the AI and Science of Science communities in promoting research and discussion on frontier topics in this area. The full-day workshop will be held in person, co-located with the 2026 ACM/IEEE-CS Joint Conference on Digital Libraries (JCDL’26).

items.title: Breaking Bottlenecks in Solid Electrolyte Discovery With Large Artificial Intelligence Models
items.excerpt: ABSTRACT Solid electrolytes (SEs) are central to next-generation metal batteries, yet their discovery remains constrained by fragmented data, limited transferability of simulations, and slow experimental iteration. Unlike catalysis, where surface reactivity dominates, SEs require simultaneous optimization of bulk ion transport, defect chemistry, mechanical integrity, and interfacial stability. Here, we outline a framework for autonomous SE discovery enabled by large artificial intelligence (AI) models, including machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) and large language models (LLMs). We discuss the evolution from static materials databases to dynamic, self-updating knowledge systems, the role of MLIPs in bridging density functional theory (DFT) and long-timescale ion migration, and the emergence of LLMs as engines for literature mining, hypothesis generation, and scientific reasoning. We further describe a closed-loop architecture integrating AI-driven candidate design, multiscale simulation, uncertainty-aware selection, and experimental validation. Such systems shift SE research from intuition-guided exploration to data-informed, self-improving cycles. We conclude by highlighting challenges in data standardization, interfacial complexity, and reproducibility, and we propose design principles for building autonomous laboratories for solid-state battery materials.

At Anthropic, coding is no longer the bottleneck to building systems or doing research. Claude is able to autonomously iterate on research loops, micro-optimize complex programs, and build new services from the ground up at a speed and scale we haven’t seen before. The bottleneck, now, is all of the developer infrastructure built for human scale: source control, builds, and CI. In May 2026, Anthropic averaged around 2,500 code changes merged per day; as of September, we merged over 30,000 per day. We don’t expect this rate of growth to slow down anytime soon; the latent demand for merging code is practically infinite, and every bottleneck we remove immediately leads to a further increase in the amount of code we produce. In order to support this growth, we built Scion, an in-house version control system, and fully migrated our monorepo from git in five months. We also built and shipped a code review surface (called Antique), code search, a rich source control IAM system, novel ways of managing and landing large amounts of reviewed code, and more, all in that same time period. In this post, we’ll focus on how we built Scion specifically. It makes for an interesting case study: Claude’s ability to write code was both what put us in this situation in the first place and how we were able to quickly build a high-quality, scalable system to deal with it. Before we explore what we built, we should acknowledge how unusual our workload is. Unsurprisingly, Anthropic uses Claude to write software far more than almost any other company, so we’re often the first to see where tools built for human scale start to strain. Source control is just one example of this. While we don’t expect many organizations to have these problems in the very near term, we suspect it won’t be too long before others who use AI coding tools experience these same pressure points, which is why we wanted to share what we built and what we learned. items.title: Reinforcement learning guided robotic platform that investigates and discovers asymmetric reactions
items.excerpt: Abstract Autonomous robotic platforms accelerate chemical discovery by coupling automated experimentation with algorithmic decision-making, but most lack integrated support for chirality and the sequential decision-making required to explore asymmetric reaction spaces with unknown reactivity and stereochemical outcomes. Here, we report a bespoke robotic platform guided by deep reinforcement learning that autonomously navigates a defined asymmetric reaction space by scouting reaction conditions, discovering chiral products, screening catalysts and mapping substrate scope. The structure-agnostic workflow is enabled by a digital twin of asymmetric catalysis, in which control policies are trained before transfer to the laboratory. We validate the approach in chiral phosphoric acid catalysis: over 30 days, the system made more than 3,000 decisions and uncovered four highly enantioselective transformations, including an axially chiral molecule and three allene syntheses, one involving the enantioselective functionalization of a pyrrolopyrrole moiety. These results highlight deep reinforcement learning-guided autonomy as a strategy for discovery in complex catalytic systems.

Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes
items.excerpt: Abstract Electrophysiological signals provide crucial and reliable information for decoding behavioral and cognitive human states. However, existing electrode interfaces are susceptible to artifacts or drift over time, thereby requiring frequent machine-learning model retraining. Here we present an end-to-end design of dry electrodes based on carbon nanotube (CNT) thin films, synthesized by a roll-to-roll floating catalyst chemical vapor deposition process. By balancing structural and electrical properties, we achieved low electrode-skin impedance, high signal fidelity, minimal motion artifacts, high breathability, and biocompatibility, outperforming the gold standard wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface demonstration, these CNT electrodes maintained stable signals and consistent task performance across 14 days using only minutes of training data and no further model retraining. To our knowledge, this is the first demonstration of a multi-day recalibration-free dry electrode system under naturalistic conditions, achieved by stable electrode-skin interface, rather than ongoing algorithmic adaptation.

items.title: Orthogonal Reversible Chemistries Affording Multistate Photoswitching in Polymers for Recyclable Intelligent Material Systems
items.excerpt: ABSTRACT The wide applications of intelligent material systems in robotics, flexible devices, AI-driven techniques, and other high-tech areas call for the development of recyclable intelligent material systems toward a sustainable future. However, intelligent material systems typically comprise multiple components with heterogeneous structures that usually interfere with or cross-contaminate each other during operation or recycling. Here, we design recyclable intelligent material systems based on orthogonal reversible chemistries, specifically photoisomerization of azobenzene and metal-ligand coordination of ruthenium complexes. We create a material, P1-Ru1, by crosslinking an azobenzene-containing polymer with a ruthenium complex. P1-Ru1 switches among multiple states that serve as structural elements, shape-changing modules, adhesives, and other components in intelligent material systems such as soft machines. Crucially, multicomponent, heterogeneous intelligent material systems constructed using different states of P1-Ru1 can be recycled via a one-pot, cross-contamination-free process because all components share the same chemical origin. This work demonstrates that orthogonal reversible chemistries make intelligent responses and recyclability compatible in complex systems. Orthogonal reversible chemistries offer a new strategy for designing recyclable intelligent material systems with multiple components and heterogeneous structures for sustainable high-tech applications.

Judges Follow the Reference: The Derivation Gap in Verifying Tool-Call Arguments
items.excerpt: Tool-call judges evaluate argument values proposed by LLM agents. We find that they accept a correct value less often when their input holds no reference for it, that is, no text that says what the value should be. This happens when the value is a default value from the function schema that the user did not mention, when it has to be inferred, or when the text it comes from was cut from the judge input. We call this drop in acceptance the derivation gap. It appears across all seven judges we evaluate, including System One models CLM and Jev. The gap is not only a truncation artifact: correct default values have the largest gap on a benchmark with no truncation. A controlled source-relocation test shows that judges follow the reference in their input: they favor a visible incorrect value over a correct value whose source is hidden. We introduce DeRef (Derived Reference): a separate model reads the full history without seeing the candidate and writes a reference for the judge. Across three benchmarks, DeRef improves overall argument AUROC for all judges tested. On the controlled test, it raises AUROC from chance or below to between 98.40 and 99.59.
items.summary: 本文提出并记录了“推导缺口”现象，即工具调用评审模型在输入中缺少明确参考答案时，更少接受正确参数值，并通过DeRef方法让独立模型生成参考以提升评审准确率。该发现可用于设计更可靠的工具调用参数评审流程，并在无截断基准和受控重定位测试中验证了缺口并非仅由截断造成；但所报告的提升幅度和AUROC区间均为原文结果，需以原始实验设置为准，不应视为对所有评审模型的普适验证。

items.title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback
items.excerpt: Test-time scaling for large language models (LLMs) can involve generating multiple candidate solutions for selection or revising an earlier attempt. To guide selection and revision, we need a verifier that can estimate candidate correctness and provide evidence of failure. In competitive programming, however, official judging systems provide authoritative verdicts under finite submission budgets, without revealing failure explanations or failing inputs. To provide informative feedback without consuming official submissions, we formulate a task in which a model judges and diagnoses a candidate program using only the problem statement and source code, with generated counterexamples serving as checkable evidence. To evaluate this task, we build USACO-JUDGE from the USACO 2026 contests, using accepted and unaccepted programs written by human experts and multiple LLMs. We then train ARBITER, a 35B mixture-of-experts (MoE) agentic verifier, with reinforcement learning in a generic execution sandbox. Training raises counterexample success on incorrect programs from 40.61% to 62.67% and mean binary verdict accuracy on USACO-JUDGE from 71.41% to 87.41%, approaching frontier verification performance. Beyond verification, ARBITER outperforms baselines in both code selection and refinement. In an IOI 2026 case study, ARBITER-guided refinement raises GPT-OSS-120B's expected score above the gold-medal threshold under the official submission limit.
items.summary: 本文提出了一种在有限官方提交预算下仅依据题面和源代码对候选程序进行判定与诊断的任务，并构建了USACO-JUDGE评测集，通过强化学习训练了35B混合专家智能体验证器ARBITER，使其以生成的反例作为可核查证据提供反馈。该工作可用于代码选择与修正等场景，但其验证性能提升与代码选择、修正方面的优势均来自作者在特定评测集上的报告，尚未经独立复现验证，且摘要未给出在更广泛编程任务或不同模型上的泛化结论。

items.title: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models
items.excerpt: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves robot foundation models (RFMs) beyond their demonstrations, but real-world deployment demands more: learning new tasks efficiently while retaining previously acquired behaviors. Existing continual RL methods on top of VLAs mitigate forgetting but rely on on-policy updates with limited forward transfer, whereas off-policy methods improve single-task sample efficiency without addressing learner persistence across tasks. We propose ACCRUE, a continual off-policy RL framework that carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, allowing each stage to reuse behavioral and value knowledge acquired through prior RL. The inherited critic adapts only on current-task transitions and guides current-task actor learning, while prior behavior is preserved by distilling the actor toward cached targets on a small number of retained episodes. Fixed visual features keep the inherited learner and its replay compatible with base-policy updates. Across contact-rich assembly sequences in simulation and on real-robot hardware, ACCRUE accelerates subsequent-task learning with near-zero forgetting and significantly reduces real-robot training time by 31.0\% to 68.5\%.
items.summary: 本文提出ACCRUE，一个持续离策略强化学习框架，通过在任务间保留轻量级actor与critic网络以复用先前习得的行为与价值知识，并借助缓存目标的策略蒸馏与固定视觉特征来兼容基座策略更新。该工作面向机器人在保留已有行为的同时高效学习新任务的研究问题，但所报告的实际机器人训练时间降低31.0%至68.5%等性能数字来自作者声明，尚需独立验证。

items.title: Enabling Token-wise Importance Sampling in Off-Policy RLVR with Proximal KL Regularization
items.excerpt: Off-policy data in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) can arise from asynchronous generation, rollout-training mismatch, and response reuse. Token-wise importance weighting avoids multiplying likelihood ratios across a response but generally biases policy gradients. We prove that, under coverage and local expressiveness conditions, full future KL credit makes the exact proximal optimizer the update's unique stationary policy, even for mixtures of older policies, without full-response weights or a fitted critic. We further establish convergence of continuous-time tabular population updates under persistent coverage and time-varying behavior policies, and a finite-sample reward guarantee for linear logistic models under additional assumptions. These results motivate Proximal KL, a practical off-policy RLVR method that separates the proximal reference from the sampling policy and replaces PPO clipping with bounded future KL credit. Across all seven matched off-policy comparisons on Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B, spanning two learning rates, response reuse, and rollout staleness, Proximal KL outperforms GRPO in micro-averaged accuracy over eight math benchmarks by up to 2.58%. A separate on-policy comparison yields comparable aggregate accuracy. In periodic-refresh experiments, Proximal KL avoids the collapses observed in PG and CISPO, exceeds GRPO's training accuracy, and reaches higher accuracy in fewer policy updates. Ablations show that token-wise correction outperforms sequence-level and unweighted controls. With token-wise correction retained, future KL feedback reduces sensitivity to the tested baseline perturbation relative to PPO clipping. A finite future horizon improves AIME24 mean@16 and pass@16 over the full tail, while fixed-policy measurements show that truncation reduces correction variance over the tested horizons.
items.summary: 本文提出 Proximal KL 方法，将近端参考分布与采样策略分离，并以有界未来 KL 信用替代 PPO 裁剪，用于离策略 RLVR 中的 token 级重要性采样。其理论结果依赖覆盖与局部表达能力等条件，有限样本奖励保证还依赖额外假设；实验仅在 Qwen3-1.7B 和 Qwen3-4B 的七个匹配离策略比较及八个数学基准上报告最高 2.58% 的微平均准确率提升，具体适用性受这些设定和假设限制。

items.title: Reading Right, Acting Wrong: Diagnosing Decision Failures of System One Models in Agent Loops
items.excerpt: System One models choose an agent's next action by scoring a supplied set of options in a single pass. This makes them fast and cheap, but when they choose wrongly there is nothing to inspect: did the model misread what the agent has seen, or read it correctly and still act wrongly? We answer behaviorally. On a frozen benchmark of agent decision states from simulated environments, customer-service policies, tool use, web navigation and coding, we pair every next-action question with factual probes about the same state, each answered independently. Across seventeen fast systems and a reasoning model, the answer is consistent: most wrong actions follow correct reading, and the more accurate a system, the more of its errors take this form. These errors are not noise; they gather on the same states across systems of every kind. Where the probed facts provably determine the action, models that read every fact still fail to combine them, and their own answers, composed by code, repair the failure. On real states, what is missing is often not a fact but the next sub-goal.
items.summary: 本文通过在同一冻结基准的智能体决策状态上并列设置下一动作选择与事实探测，行为性地诊断了System One模型在智能体循环中的决策失败，发现多数错误动作发生在正确读取之后。该诊断方法可用于区分读取错误与决策组合失败，但原文明确显示模型即使读取全部可确定动作的事实仍可能无法组合，且在真实状态中缺失的常是下一子目标而非某个事实。

items.title: Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion
items.excerpt: Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates local corrections from the student's interval-mean prediction. We further repel the student from weaker teacher predictions, providing a lightweight mechanism for avoiding undesirable modes. The resulting framework, Simplified Matching Distillation (SMD), remains entirely regression-based, requires neither online score estimation nor adversarial training, and leaves the deployed generator unchanged. We evaluate SMD on image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio--video generation, scaling to 33 billion parameters. At 4-NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step baselines and surpasses multi-step teachers on several benchmarks. It also supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation.

items.title: Model-Based Online Decision Making via Generative Trajectory Planning
items.excerpt: Online decision-making faces a tension between efficient inference and long-horizon reasoning. Value-based methods rely on short-horizon bootstrapping that limits the propagation of long-term information, while trajectory optimization methods plan explicitly but must solve a high-dimensional optimization problem at every decision step. We propose Generative Trajectory Planning (GTP), a model-based framework that addresses this tension by learning a generative model as a proposal distribution over action sequences. Instead of optimizing sequences from scratch, GTP samples candidate sequences from a diffusion prior and refines them using learned dynamics, reward, and value models, enabling efficient trajectory-level reasoning. Across continuous control and long-horizon manipulation tasks, GTP matches or exceeds state-of-the-art model-free, diffusion-policy, and model-based baselines, and remains stable in regimes where strong baselines degrade. Our results suggest that generative models are best understood not as policies, but as structured proposal distributions for planning, offering a new perspective on how to integrate generative modeling with model-based decision-making.
items.summary: 本文提出生成式轨迹规划（GTP），一种基于模型的框架，通过将生成模型学习为动作序列上的提议分布，从扩散先验中采样候选序列并利用学习到的动力学、奖励和价值模型进行精化，而非从零优化序列。该工作面向在线决策中高效推理与长时程推理之间的张力，在连续控制和长时程操作任务上报告了与无模型、扩散策略及基于模型基线相当或更优的表现，并在强基线退化时保持稳定，但上述性能声明来自作者报告，尚未经独立验证。

items.title: Unlocking Structured Pruning for Reasoning Language Models via Attention-Preserving MLP Trimming
items.excerpt: Structured pruning reduces LLM inference costs by removing model components to produce smaller dense models. However, existing methods can cause reasoning performance to collapse on long-form reasoning tasks such as AIME. We propose LayerTrim, a training-free structured pruning method that identifies redundant decoder layers and selectively trims their MLP features while preserving attention and decoder depth. LayerTrim is the first training-free structured pruning method designed to preserve long-form reasoning without gradients or recovery training. Across three reasoning language models and five benchmarks, LayerTrim outperforms existing structured pruning methods in most evaluated settings, improving average accuracy by up to 21.4 percentage points over RESP. On Qwen3-14B, LayerTrim achieves 1.24times faster prefill and 19.7\% lower peak GPU memory than the dense model, while better preserving reasoning ability. It also achieves the shortest average generation length among evaluated pruned models, while retaining the highest average accuracy. These results demonstrate that LayerTrim improves reasoning efficiency through both structural compression and reduced token generation.
items.summary: 本文提出LayerTrim，一种无需训练的 structured pruning 方法，通过识别冗余解码层并选择性裁剪其MLP特征，同时保留注意力与解码深度，以缓解现有结构化剪枝在AIME等长程推理任务上的性能崩溃。若原文结论成立，该方法可为推理语言模型在无需梯度或恢复训练的条件下压缩模型、改善推理效率提供参考，但其跨模型与基准的优势及速度、显存收益仍需独立验证。

items.title: PreciseCoder: Faithful and Generalizable Debugging Beyond Unit-Test Rewards
items.excerpt: Reinforcement learning (RL) from unit tests is the common recipe for post-training code models, but a unit test only asks whether the final program passes. We analyze what this unit-test-only reward teaches a model during debugging and find that, while it raises pass rates, it also teaches the model to edit more and to hallucinate bugs in code that is already correct. We introduce PreciseCoder, a training algorithm that augments the unit-test reward with a signal for semantically verified, localized edits, which correlates with smaller edits and higher pass rates. On 4B, 9B, and 27B models, PreciseCoder reduces the average number of edit lines from 7-15to 3 at a pass rate on par with unit-test-only training. Trained only on single-line bugs, PreciseCoder can generalize to repository-level program repair, where it resolves more issues with smaller patches. Its precision also transfers from weaker to stronger models: given the reasoning trace of a 9B PreciseCoder model, frontier models such as GPT-5.6 Sol and Qwen3.8-Max gain 4.6-12.4 points in edit precision with no additional training. Linguistic analysis of the thinking traces shows that our reward encourages the model to reason about individual lines, name the buggy ones, and form consistent bug hypotheses.
items.summary: 本文提出PreciseCoder训练算法，在单元测试奖励之外加入经语义验证的局部编辑信号，并在4B、9B和27B模型上报告其将平均编辑行数从7-15行降至3行且通过率与仅用单元测试训练相当，同时声称仅用单行缺陷训练即可泛化到仓库级程序修复。该工作面向代码模型调试的后训练研究，但原文结论来自公司声明或论文自述，尚未经独立验证，且其精度迁移与泛化效果需在相应模型和基准上进一步复现确认。

items.title: Decoding the Impact of Solvent Hydrogen-Bonding Networks on Nanozyme Activity via Machine Learning Potentials
items.excerpt: Precise mechanistic insights into the chemical reactions at solid-liquid interfaces are crucial for advancing functional nanomaterials, such as enzyme-mimicking nanocatalysts known as nanozymes. However, conventional periodic density functional theory (DFT) calculations, usually performed under vacuum conditions, can systematically underestimate reaction barriers, leading to discrepancies between computational predictions and the catalytic performance of nanomaterials in aqueous environments. Here, we propose a deep potential (DP)-based strategy that integrates DFT, ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), and active learning to resolve solvent-mediated reaction kinetics. Using hydrogen peroxide dissociation on Au(111) as a prototypical model reaction for nanozyme activity, we develop a DP model that show comparable accuracy to DFT calculations, enabling efficient identification of transition states in explicit solvents. Calculations using this model have demonstrated that the aqueous hydrogen-bonding network significantly increases the energy barrier for $H_2O_2$ dissociation by 0.58 eV, the experimentally observed low activity of gold nanoparticles in aqueous media. This approach provides a robust framework to decode solvent effects on chemical reactions at solid-liquid interfaces, which is valuable for advancing the rational design of functional nanocatalysts such as nanozymes.
items.summary: 本文提出了一种结合密度泛函理论、从头算分子动力学与主动学习的深度势策略，并以Au(111)表面过氧化氢解离为模型反应，构建了精度与DFT相当、可在显式溶剂中高效识别过渡态的深度势模型，计算表明水相氢键网络使该解离能垒升高0.58 eV。该框架可用于解析固液界面溶剂对化学反应的影响，从而辅助纳米酶等功能纳米催化剂的理性设计；上述0.58 eV等数值与机理结论来自所提供摘要，尚未经独立验证，且摘要未说明模型在其他体系或条件下的适用性限制。

items.title: Synergistic regulation of temperature and primary knock-on atom energy on irradiation damage evolution in tantalum: A molecular dynamics study.
items.excerpt: Tantalum is a candidate material for advanced nuclear systems, but its irradiation damage mechanisms remain unclear. Using molecular dynamics with the UNEP-v1-ZBL machine-learning potential, we simulated BCC Ta under 1-50 keV PKA irradiation at 300-900 K. Results show that threshold displacement energy decreases with temperature and exhibits anisotropy. Defect evolution displays strong energy-temperature coupling: low-energy cascades (≤5 keV) follow monotonic displacement chain behavior, while high-energy cascades (≥15 keV) are governed by competition between thermal spike formation and energy dissipation. Interstitial clusters outnumber vacancy clusters due to low migration energy and ⟨111⟩ diffusion. Cascade morphology controls final damage accumulation by modulating defect spatial distribution. These atomic-scale insights provide theoretical foundations for accurate damage modeling and radiation-resistant material design.
items.summary: 本文用分子动力学与UNEP-v1-ZBL机器学习势模拟了300–900 K、1–50 keV初级撞出原子能量下BCC钽的辐照损伤演化，报告了阈位移能随温度降低并呈各向异性，以及低能与高能级联在缺陷演化上的不同能量—温度耦合行为。该工作可为辐照损伤建模和抗辐照材料设计提供原子尺度参考，但其结论基于特定势函数与模拟条件，属于模拟结果而非实验验证。
